the resistance of melanoma to OSM/IL-6 correlates with poor prognosis for stage III patients treated by TIL, that OSM/IL6 sensitivity correlates with TIL production of these cytokines before TIL injection, that OSM is a potent inhibitor of melanoma cell proliferation in vitro and in vivo in immunodeficient mice. © 2008 The Authors.

(a) responsiveness of melanoma cells towards anti‐prolferative cytokines is an independent prognostic factor for survival of stage III (lympnodes metastases) melanoma patients treated by adoptive transfer with tumour‐ infiltrating lymphocytes, and (b) responsiveness of melanocytes to anti‐proliferaive cytokines is not related to other known prognostics factors for early stage (T2 and T3) melanoma patients.
OSM/IL6‐resistant metastatic melanoma cells are resistant to TIL‐induced apoptosis, and that this resistance is a new prognostic factor for stage III melanoma.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of a high number of TILs, the presence of a low number of CD8 + T cells and a high number of CD4 + T cells, and the presence of CD8 + /CD4 + ratio of 1.5 or less, all are prognostic indicators of poor prognosis for patients with stage III melanoma.

OSM/IL-6 resistance of melanomas is a new mechanism of resistance to TIL immunotherapy that can be added to the known prognostic markers of melanoma, and could be used for the design of more specific anti-cancer therapies.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the responsiveness of melanoma cells for OSM and/or IL‐ 6 is a new escape mechanism that is relevant in TIL treatment and could be also relevant for other immunotherapy protocols.

OSM and IL-6 sensitivity of melanomas is a new prognostic factor of survival for stage III melanoma treated with TIL, and that this resistance mechanism of melanoma cells is related with the lack of production of OSM and IL6 by tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes before their injection.
we have shown that resistance of melanoma to OSM and IL6 is a prognostic factor for stage III melanoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the responsiveness of melanoma cells towards OSM/IL-6 is an independent prognostic factor in patients with stage III melanoma treated with tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes.
resistance of melanoma to OSM and IL6 could be used as a prognostic factor for stage III melanoma.
the responsiveness of cancer cells (in this case melanoma cells) to anti‐prolifera‐tive cytokines such as IL‐6 and OSM may be a factor to consider in the prognosis of melanoma patients.
